newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean civilians engage in anti-biochemical drill.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean civilians engage in anti-biochemical drill.

text.p: South Korean civilians, police and fire-fighters fought off a mock biochemical attack on Tuesday as part of a 12-day military exercise to prepare for possible aggression by communist North Korea.
The drill was the first joint military-civilian exercise of the annual war games by the U.S. and South Korean troops codenamed Ulchi Focus Lens, which kicked off on Monday.
Red and yellow smoke released into the air in a Seoul park signalled the mock attack which prompted more than 400 participants, some in full rubber suits and gas masks, to scramble to the defence.
"People are fainting in the park from an enemy chemical bomb," roared loud speakers on military trucks as water was sprayed to diffuse the mock gases.
The annual manoeuvres featured computer-simulated war games and involved tens of thousands of South Korean troops as well as 16,500 U.S. soldiers, military officials said.
A statement by the Capital Defence Command which took part in the anti-biochemical exercise said the drill would serve to awaken civilians to the dangers of possible terrorist attack.
The air force also took part in the drill. Fighter jets on regular missions were called back to base to reload weapons to help suppress the mock enemy infiltration.
In parallel with the war games, due to last until August 29, South Korea will hold a government-level command post exercise and air-raid drills involving citizens.

Seoul officials have said the exercises had long been planned and had nothing to do with four-nation peace talks being arranged by the two Koreas, the United States and China to work out an agreement for permanent peace on the peninsula.
North Korea has criticised the United States and South Korea for planning Ulchi Focus Lens, labelling the exercise "an extremely threatening act".

Seoul and Washington have carried out joint military exercises every year since 1976. In March they cancelled larger military exercises, Team Spirit, in a goodwill gesture to coax North Korea towards the four-party peace talks.
Team Spirit, which used to be held annually, has been a major source of inter-Korean friction, with the North calling it preparation for an invasion. The drills were last held in 1993.

About 655,000 South Korean troops, backed by 37,000 U.S. servicemen, confront North Korea's 1.1 million-strong army across the world's last Cold War frontier, the legacy of the 1950-53 Korea War which ended in a truce rather than a peace treaty.
